location.section: ## Thresholding a smooth Gaussian input produces place fields {#sec:PLACE-GP}
location.paragraph_opening: Three assumptions have different jobs. [**Stationarity**]{.definition-term custom-style="Definition Term"} means that mo

edits.before: Three assumptions have different jobs. [**Stationarity**]{.definition-term custom-style="Definition Term"} means that moving the observation window does not change the map's probability law. Here it gives a constant mean and a covariance $C(x,y)=C(y-x)$ that depends on separation. It does not say that a particular map is flat. [**Isotropy**]{.definition-term custom-style="Definition Term"} means that rotating the separation does not change the covariance: in several dimensions, $C(\Delta x)$ depends only on $\|\Delta x\|$. It rules out a preferred direction in the model's statistics. Stationarity alone does not imply isotropy. Finally, smoothness controls whether the map has well defined spatial derivatives. Crossing calculations below require differentiable sample functions and nondegenerate joint distributions: the relevant vector of heights and derivatives must have an invertible covariance matrix, rather than obey an exact linear constraint. Peak calculations require second derivatives and enough regularity to control their local approximation. A Gaussian distribution of values does not guarantee this smoothness. For example, a covariance proportional to $e^{-|x-y|/b}$ has a sharp corner at zero separation and does not supply the differentiable paths assumed below.
edits.after:
Three assumptions have different jobs:

- [**Stationarity**]{.definition-term custom-style="Definition Term"} means that moving the observation window does not change the map's probability law. Here it gives a constant mean and a covariance $C(x,y)=C(y-x)$ that depends on separation. It does not say that a particular map is flat.
- [**Isotropy**]{.definition-term custom-style="Definition Term"} means that rotating the separation does not change the covariance: in several dimensions, $C(\Delta x)$ depends only on $\|\Delta x\|$. It rules out a preferred direction in the model's statistics. Stationarity alone does not imply isotropy.
- [**Smoothness**]{.definition-term custom-style="Definition Term"} controls whether the map has well defined spatial derivatives. Crossing calculations require differentiable sample functions and nondegenerate joint distributions: the relevant vector of heights and derivatives must have an invertible covariance matrix, rather than obey an exact linear constraint. Peak calculations require second derivatives and enough regularity to control their local approximation.

A Gaussian distribution of values does not guarantee this smoothness. For example, a covariance proportional to $e^{-|x-y|/b}$ has a sharp corner at zero separation and does not supply the differentiable paths assumed below.
edits.rationale: Expose the independent assumptions and keep each with the calculation it supports. Mark the actual smoothness explanation.
edits.preserved_premise_or_limit: Stationarity is distinct from isotropy and smoothness; differentiability, nondegeneracy, second derivative requirements and counterexample remain.

location.section: ## Holes distinguish maps with the same field count {#sec:PLACE-TOPOLOGY}
location.paragraph_opening: The [**Euler characteristic**]{.definition-term custom-style="Definition Term"}, written $\chi$, combines these counts.

edits.before: The [**Euler characteristic**]{.definition-term custom-style="Definition Term"}, written $\chi$, combines these counts. In 1D it equals the number of connected active intervals. In 2D it is the number of connected components minus the number of independent holes. Three disjoint disks have $\chi=3$; one connected ring has $\chi=1-1=0$. In 3D it is components minus independent tunnels plus enclosed cavities. A solid ball has $\chi=1$, a solid ring has $\chi=0$, and a hollow spherical shell has $\chi=2$. These counts are the first three [**Betti numbers**]{.definition-term custom-style="Definition Term"}: numbers of independent components, loops, and cavities, respectively.[^p3-ec-source]
edits.after:
The [**Euler characteristic**]{.definition-term custom-style="Definition Term"}, written $\chi$, combines these counts differently in each dimension:

- In 1D it equals the number of connected active intervals.
- In 2D it is the number of connected components minus the number of independent holes. Three disjoint disks have $\chi=3$; one connected ring has $\chi=1-1=0$.
- In 3D it is components minus independent tunnels plus enclosed cavities. A solid ball has $\chi=1$, a solid ring has $\chi=0$, and a hollow spherical shell has $\chi=2$.

These counts are the first three [**Betti numbers**]{.definition-term custom-style="Definition Term"}: numbers of independent components, loops, and cavities, respectively.[^p3-ec-source]
edits.rationale: Make the dimension-specific rules easy to compare without separating them from their examples.
edits.preserved_premise_or_limit: Signed count, dimensional distinctions, examples, Betti explanation and citation retained exactly.

location.section: ## What was fitted and what was tested {#sec:PLACE-DATA}
location.paragraph_opening: The processing choices affect the quantities being compared. Bat maps were rectified at about 0.5 Hz for denoising. The

edits.before: The processing choices affect the quantities being compared. Bat maps were rectified at about 0.5 Hz for denoising. The 3D maps, sampled in 10 cm bins, also received a median filter. Fields larger than three standard deviations above mean 3D volume were removed as possible merges, including from slice analyses. Peak counting excluded incomplete boundary fields and used a range of smoothing widths. The 1D rate versus width comparison used an additional 1 Hz cutoff. These decisions can remove small components, alter peaks, and change tails. They belong to the definition of the analyzed fields.[^p3-processing]
edits.after:
The processing choices affect the quantities being compared:

- Bat maps were rectified at about 0.5 Hz for denoising.
- The 3D maps, sampled in 10 cm bins, also received a median filter.
- Fields larger than three standard deviations above mean 3D volume were removed as possible merges, including from slice analyses.
- Peak counting excluded incomplete boundary fields and used a range of smoothing widths.
- The 1D rate versus width comparison used an additional 1 Hz cutoff.

These decisions can remove small components, alter peaks, and change tails. They belong to the definition of the analyzed fields.[^p3-processing]
edits.rationale: Reveal five independent processing choices before interpreting their effects on the comparison.
edits.preserved_premise_or_limit: Every measurement condition, cutoff, boundary exclusion, possible-merge qualification and processing consequence is preserved.
